solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Likewise, newspaper to support book

parts.note: 'so' can mean likewise, as in 'so do I'
FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, then says a newspaper will lend its weight to promoting a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback edition is a type of book bound in flexible covers.

clue.text: Creator's filling tin with the Spanish fruitcake

indicators.note: filling means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
the creator of the puzzle is the setter, so 'creator is' gives I'm
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A baker's creation is a tin filled with a Spanish fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks of themself as I or ME; here 'Creator's' is 'creator is', so I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A simnel is a rich fruitcake with marzipan, traditionally eaten in Britain at Easter.

clue.text: Rat-catcher runs repeatedly into foundations

indicators.note: into places the doubled letter inside the word for foundations

parts.note: feet are the foundations one stands on, or the base of a structure

indicators.note: repeatedly means the abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rodent-catcher keeps darting into a building's foundations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrets were long kept for hunting, flushing out rats and rabbits from burrows.

clue.text: Cry from a German hurt at back between shoulders

indicators.note: between puts the German article and final letter inside the verb for shoulders

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it, so shoulders gives bears
ein is German for 'a'

indicators.note: at back takes the final letter of 'hurt'

explanation.surface: A German weeps from a pain in the back between the shoulder blades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoulders' looks like a body part but is a verb; its synonym splits B...EARS around EINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to weep, which is to shed tears, a state the phrase describes.

clue.text: Firm ordered Neil to safeguard work's capital once

parts.note: firm means steady, unchanging

indicators.note: to safeguard is to protect by enclosing, so the rearranged name surrounds the work
ordered means the letters of the name Neil are rearranged

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A firm tells Neil to protect the capital invested in a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' makes INLE from Neil, which wraps around OP to give INOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantinople was the capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires before it was renamed Istanbul.

clue.text: Head girl that provides zest in the kitchen?

definitions.text: that provides zest in the kitchen?

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: A head girl is praised as the one who livens things up in the school kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head girl' reads as one school title, but it splits into two pieces; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This grated spice adds flavour, or zest, to cooking, so it livens up kitchen dishes.

clue.text: Custom in European Union to raise outside flag

indicators.note: outside means the reversed letters go around the word for flag
to raise in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EU is the European Union
to flag is to droop, or sag

explanation.surface: It's EU practice to fly a flag outside a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established practice or habit, especially in how language is used.

clue.text: Motorway extremely difficult to patrol closely — at this hour?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: to patrol is to go around, so the outer letters enclose the next piece
extremely takes the outermost letters of 'difficult'

parts.note: nigh means near, close by

explanation.surface: Police find a motorway hard to patrol at close quarters at such a late hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway, its 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is the hour suggested, the time when patrols are hardest.

clue.text: Dicky may need to go beyond garden's entrance to see moon

indicators.note: to go beyond means the rearranged letters come after the opening letter
the entrance of a word is its first letter
dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone with a dodgy heart may need to walk past a garden gate to see the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter, named after Zeus's cupbearer.

clue.text: Hold dear Linda's comic novel

parts.note: to treasure something is to hold it dear

indicators.note: comic means the letters of Linda's are played around with

explanation.surface: Someone cherishes Linda's funny book.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 adventure novel of pirates and buried gold.

clue.text: Red woolly thing returned by Scotsman

indicators.note: returned means the word for the woolly animal is read backwards

parts.note: a ram is a woolly male sheep
X is the multiplication sign, as in three by four
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sends back a red woolly garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red woolly thing' looks like a jumper, but 'Red' alone is the definition, in its political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a communist, a follower of the doctrines of Karl Marx.

clue.text: Managed to obtain symbol of magic from Africa

indicators.note: to obtain is to take in, so the word for managed holds the other piece

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives ran
a wand is the emblem of a conjuror or wizard

explanation.surface: A conjuror managed to get hold of a magic emblem from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Rwanda comes from a country in central Africa.

clue.text: Result: 50-50, with time added on

indicators.note: added on says the time letter is attached at the end

parts.note: fifty-fifty odds or a draw are even

explanation.surface: A football match ends level and goes into added time.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an outcome, as in 'in the event', meaning the result as it turned out.

clue.text: In working group (male), there's a prize for wagging — small bone

indicators.note: 'In' puts the shuffled letters inside the letters for the working group

parts.note: TU is a trade union, a group of workers

indicators.note: wagging means moving to and fro, so the letters of 'a prize' are shaken up

explanation.surface: A works committee hands out a prize to a man for playing truant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wagging' here suggests skiving off school (to wag it is British slang for truancy), but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapezium is one of the carpal bones of the wrist, a small bone near the thumb.

clue.text: RU Lion trained inside ground, given very little food

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the word for ground

parts.note: food that is ground is crushed, or mashed

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters of 'RU Lion' are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby union side's British Lion trains on a pitch while barely fed.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union, and the British and Irish Lions are its touring team; NOURIL, the rearrangement, goes in after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone underfed suffers from poor nutrition, the state of being deprived of proper food.

clue.text: Whatever happens, Ian will be shocked by New York state

indicators.note: being shocked jolts the three letters of the name into a new order

parts.note: a case is a state of affairs, as in 'the case'

explanation.surface: Come what may, Ian is going to be appalled by New York State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York state' reads as one place, but it splits into New York and state.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means regardless, no matter what occurs.

clue.text: Pretty Parisian wearing waterproof coat, takes a piece of earthenware

indicators.note: wearing means the French word goes inside the coat

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat
joli is French for pretty
the letter A is added on

explanation.surface: A pretty Frenchwoman in a raincoat carries off a bit of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiolica is tin-glazed Italian earthenware, so an item of it is a piece of pottery.

clue.text: Paint large bird near son feeding cat

indicators.note: near says the bird sits next to the following piece

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: feeding means the letter goes into the word for cat

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Someone paints a big bird near their son as he feeds the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based household wall paint.

clue.text: When recalling soldiers chilled by the air of gunfire, forever

indicators.note: by says one piece sits beside the next
recalling means calling back, so the letters for soldiers run backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
gunfire leaves a smoky mist hanging in the air
something chilled is iced
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always, forever

explanation.surface: A wartime memory of troops frozen in the smoke of the guns, for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' alone is the definition: the answer is a date, an occasion. 'recalling soldiers' looks like part of it but is the reversal; 'by' joins the last two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Armistice Day, 11 November, is a date, so it answers the question 'when?'.

clue.text: Male after mostly fast food

indicators.note: mostly means the word for fast loses its last letter

parts.note: quick means fast
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man goes after some fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' looks like the definition, but 'fast' is wordplay and 'food' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury tart of eggs and cream, a kind of food.

clue.text: Menace, at that point, releasing initial energy

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of a letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: thereat is an old word meaning at that place or time

indicators.note: initial takes the first letter of 'energy'

explanation.surface: A danger at that moment, once the first burst of power is let go.
explanation.walkthrough: THEREAT has two Es; releasing the first leaves THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is something that threatens danger, an intimidation.

clue.text: Old boy mostly annoyed with locums appearing regularly forgetful

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for annoyed

parts.note: livid means furious

indicators.note: appearing regularly takes every other letter of 'locums'

explanation.surface: A former pupil is irritated that stand-in doctors keep forgetting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware or unmindful of something is a close synonym of being forgetful.

clue.text: Light fabric one used to block rodent

indicators.note: used to block means the letter is put into the rodent's name to plug it

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item is used to block a rodent hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a thin, semi-transparent cotton or silk fabric used for curtains.

clue.text: Juvenile, seeing heartland in mayhem, keeps away

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the centre of mayhem wraps around the next piece
the heartland of a word is its middle, so the central letters of 'mayhem' are taken

parts.note: away means out, as in 'she is out'

explanation.surface: A young person sees chaos in the country's heartland and steers clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, someone not yet adult, which is what a juvenile is.

clue.text: First sign

definitions.meaning: the adjective meaning occurring at the beginning
the verb meaning to mark a document with one's own monogram

explanation.surface: Two words that read as an instruction to put a signature down before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means beginning; the verb means marking a page with the leading letters of one's name.

clue.text: Cooker placed by posh cook briefly on the left

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy range cooker
U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'

indicators.note: briefly means the word for cook loses its last letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A cooker is installed next to a smart chef's station, positioned to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is the classic cast-iron stove of a British country kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means to or on the left-hand side.

clue.text: European city branch recruiting new man

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in, so the word for branch holds the other pieces

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of an organisation or river
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A firm's European office takes on a new employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem is a city in the eastern Netherlands, famous for its 1944 bridge battle.

clue.text: Poster in this place alongside set of books is sticking

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a poster
here means in this place
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An advert placed here next to a shelf of books won't come unstuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherent as an adjective means clinging or attached, as glue makes things stick.
